```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
```

```{r setup}
library(mysteryroster)
```

In 2013 the HHS Office of Inspector General compared NPPES with PECOS on
three axes (*Improvements Are Needed To Ensure Provider Enumeration and
Medicare Enrollment Data Are Accurate, Complete, and Consistent*,
OEI-07-09-00440). **Accuracy** needed providers to verify their own records.
**Completeness** (is each field populated) and **consistency** (do two
databases say the same thing about the same NPI) need no truth at all. OIG
found 97.4% of providers inconsistent on at least one of ten fields, with
practice ZIP mismatched for 88.6%.

This vignette runs the two truth-free axes across six simulated
practice-location sources for nurse-midwives, using the package's OIG-style
functions. It improves on the original report in four ways:

- every field is reported separately, not only "any of ten fields";
- a midwife missing from one source is never counted as a disagreement;
- each pair is flagged when its two sources share an upstream feed;
- each disagreement rate gives a floor on error that needs no truth.

## The data

The six sources mirror the structure of a real midwifery audit (the
`midwifery` repository's `analysis/oig_style_source_consistency.R`), but every
record here is simulated. The identifiers are placeholders. Coverage and
agreement rates are set to land roughly where that audit's aggregate results
did, and no person-level data is used.

- **NPPES** lists every midwife, one location each.
- **PECOS** reassignment records list the *organization* a midwife bills
  through, sometimes several. This is the mechanism OIG's Appendix A blamed
  for its practice-ZIP mismatch.
- **DAC** is built from PECOS enrollment but lists practice locations.
- **Open Payments** gives one recipient address per payment.
- **Doximity** often copies NPPES.
- **Healthgrades** lists one or more offices.

```{r simulate}
set.seed(20261108)
n <- 3000
ids <- sprintf("M%04d", seq_len(n))
states <- c("CO", "NM", "TX", "CA", "NY", "OR", "WA", "FL")
zip_pool <- lapply(seq_along(states), function(i) sprintf("%05d", 10000 * i + sample(0:9999, 40)))
names(zip_pool) <- states
home_state <- sample(states, n, TRUE)
home_zip <- vapply(home_state, function(s) sample(zip_pool[[s]], 1), "")

# Each listed location keeps the midwife's home ZIP with probability p_zip,
# moves to another ZIP in the same state up to p_state, and otherwise to
# another state.
draw <- function(idx, p_zip, p_state) {
  u <- runif(length(idx))
  st <- home_state[idx]
  zp <- home_zip[idx]
  same_state <- u >= p_zip & u < p_state
  zp[same_state] <- vapply(st[same_state], function(s) sample(zip_pool[[s]], 1), "")
  moved <- u >= p_state
  st[moved] <- vapply(st[moved], function(s) sample(setdiff(states, s), 1), "")
  zp[moved] <- vapply(st[moved], function(s) sample(zip_pool[[s]], 1), "")
  data.frame(npi = ids[idx], state = st, zip = zp)
}
listed <- function(share) sample(n, round(share * n))
extra <- function(idx, share) sample(idx, round(share * length(idx)))

nppes <- draw(seq_len(n), 0.92, 0.97)
pecos_ids <- listed(0.47)
pecos <- rbind(draw(pecos_ids, 0.18, 0.86), draw(extra(pecos_ids, 0.30), 0.15, 0.80))
dac_ids <- listed(0.41)
dac <- rbind(draw(dac_ids, 0.55, 0.92), draw(extra(dac_ids, 0.25), 0.40, 0.90))
op_ids <- listed(0.34)
op <- rbind(draw(op_ids, 0.84, 0.97), draw(extra(op_ids, 0.25), 0.80, 0.97))
dox_ids <- listed(0.39)
doximity <- nppes[dox_ids, ]
reseeded <- runif(length(dox_ids)) > 0.85
doximity[reseeded, ] <- draw(dox_ids[reseeded], 0.60, 0.92)
hg_ids <- listed(0.50)
healthgrades <- rbind(draw(hg_ids, 0.80, 0.96), draw(extra(hg_ids, 0.40), 0.60, 0.92))

# A few blank and malformed fields, so completeness has something to find.
nppes$zip[sample(n, 15)] <- "802"
nppes$state[sample(n, 10)] <- ""
healthgrades$state[sample(nrow(healthgrades), 40)] <- ""

raw <- list(nppes = nppes, pecos = pecos, dac = dac, open_payments = op,
            doximity = doximity, healthgrades = healthgrades)
sapply(raw, function(d) c(rows = nrow(d), midwives = length(unique(d$npi))))
```

## Declare fields and lineage first

`attribute_field_dictionary()` records what each field means and which
sources share lineage. DAC is derived from PECOS enrollment, so the two form
one lineage group. Nothing in the data can reveal that; it has to be
declared.

```{r dictionary}
fields <- data.frame(
  attribute = c("practice_state", "practice_zip5"),
  definition = c("Two-letter practice state", "First five digits of the practice ZIP"),
  location_role = "practice",
  normalizer = c("state_abb", "zip5")
)
dictionary <- attribute_field_dictionary(fields, sources = names(raw),
                                         lineage_groups = list(cms_enrollment = c("pecos", "dac")))
unique(dictionary[, c("source", "lineage")])
```

## Completeness: absent, blank, malformed, usable

OIG's completeness arm asked whether each field was populated in records
that exist. `attribute_record_presence()` keeps three reasons for a missing
value apart: the record is absent, the field was never in the extract, or the
field is blank. It treats any non-blank value as populated, so a
malformed-value check is added on top.

```{r presence}
coverage <- expand.grid(id = ids, source = names(raw), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
coverage$year <- 2026
coverage$record_present <- mapply(function(i, s) i %in% raw[[s]]$npi, coverage$id, coverage$source)
coverage$record_status <- ifelse(coverage$record_present, "present", "not_in_source")

claims <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(raw), function(s) {
  d <- raw[[s]]
  rbind(data.frame(npi = d$npi, year = 2026, source = s, attribute = "practice_state", value = d$state),
        data.frame(npi = d$npi, year = 2026, source = s, attribute = "practice_zip5", value = d$zip))
}))
claims <- claims[nzchar(claims$value), ]

source_fields <- expand.grid(year = 2026, source = names(raw), attribute = fields$attribute,
                             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
source_fields$field_available <- TRUE

presence <- attribute_record_presence(coverage, dictionary, source_fields, claims)
with(presence[presence$attribute == "practice_zip5", ], table(source, field_status))
```

```{r usable}
usable <- lapply(raw, function(d) {
  data.frame(npi = d$npi,
             practice_state = ifelse(d$state %in% state.abb, d$state, NA),
             practice_zip5 = ifelse(grepl("^[0-9]{5}$", d$zip), d$zip, NA))
})
completeness <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(raw), function(s) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(fields$attribute, function(a) {
    p <- presence[presence$source == s & presence$attribute == a, ]
    ok <- unique(usable[[s]]$npi[!is.na(usable[[s]][[a]])])
    data.frame(source = s, attribute = a,
               absent = sum(!p$record_present),
               blank = sum(p$field_status == "field_value_missing"),
               malformed = sum(p$field_status == "populated") - length(ok),
               usable = length(ok))
  }))
}))
completeness[completeness$attribute == "practice_zip5", ]
```

```{r fig-completeness, fig.height = 3.8, fig.alt = "Stacked horizontal bars, one per source, splitting the simulated cohort into midwives absent from the source, present with a blank or malformed ZIP, and present with a usable ZIP."}
z <- completeness[completeness$attribute == "practice_zip5", ]
m <- t(as.matrix(z[, c("usable", "blank", "malformed", "absent")]))
colnames(m) <- z$source
fills <- c("#1b7837", "#fdb863", "#e66101", "grey80")
op_par <- par(mar = c(7, 8, 2, 1))
barplot(m[, rev(seq_len(ncol(m)))], horiz = TRUE, las = 1, border = NA, col = fills,
        main = "Practice ZIP5: mostly absent, rarely blank")
title(xlab = "Midwives in the cohort", line = 2.2)
legend("bottom", inset = c(0, -0.62), xpd = TRUE, horiz = TRUE, bty = "n", cex = 0.8,
       legend = c("usable", "blank", "malformed", "absent"), fill = fills, border = NA)
par(op_par)
```

Only NPPES lists everyone. For every other source, the gap is mostly
midwives the source does not list, which is a question of coverage, not data
quality. Fields missing from records that do exist, the thing OIG actually
measured, are rare.

## Consistency: any-match, field by field

OIG counted a provider with several licenses or addresses as consistent if
*any* value matched. `attribute_set_agreement()` compares each source's set
of usable values for a midwife and returns both the any-match rule
(`any_shared`) and the strict rule (`same_set`). Only midwives with a usable
value in *both* sources enter the denominator.

```{r set-agreement}
set_input <- function(attr) {
  lapply(usable, function(d) {
    v <- unique(d[!is.na(d[[attr]]), c("npi", attr)])
    v$year <- 2026
    v
  })
}
agree <- rbind(
  transform(attribute_set_agreement_summary(attribute_set_agreement(set_input("practice_state"), "practice_state")),
            attribute = "practice_state"),
  transform(attribute_set_agreement_summary(attribute_set_agreement(set_input("practice_zip5"), "practice_zip5")),
            attribute = "practice_zip5")
)
ci <- wilson_ci(agree$n_any_shared, agree$n_compared, as_percent = TRUE)
agree$pct_any <- round(100 * agree$pct_any_shared, 1)
agree$ci <- sprintf("%.1f-%.1f", ci$ci_low, ci$ci_high)
agree$pct_same <- round(100 * agree$pct_same_set, 1)
agree$lineage <- ifelse(paste(pmin(agree$source_a, agree$source_b), pmax(agree$source_a, agree$source_b)) == "dac pecos",
                        "shared (CMS enrollment)",
                        ifelse(agree$source_a == "nppes" & agree$source_b %in% c("doximity", "healthgrades") |
                                 agree$source_b == "nppes" & agree$source_a %in% c("doximity", "healthgrades"),
                               "possible NPPES seeding", "separately collected"))
agree[agree$attribute == "practice_zip5",
      c("source_a", "source_b", "lineage", "n_compared", "pct_any", "ci", "pct_same")]
```

```{r fig-heatmap, fig.height = 4.2, fig.alt = "Two six-by-six heatmaps of any-match agreement between every pair of sources. Practice state agreement is high in every cell; practice ZIP5 agreement is much lower, and lowest in every cell involving PECOS."}
pair_matrix <- function(attr) {
  s <- names(raw)
  m <- matrix(NA, length(s), length(s), dimnames = list(s, s))
  a <- agree[agree$attribute == attr, ]
  m[cbind(a$source_a, a$source_b)] <- a$pct_any
  m[cbind(a$source_b, a$source_a)] <- a$pct_any
  m
}
draw_heat <- function(m, title) {
  k <- nrow(m)
  pal <- colorRampPalette(c("#b2182b", "#f7f7f7", "#2166ac"))(101)
  image(seq_len(k), seq_len(k), t(m[k:1, ]), col = pal, zlim = c(0, 100),
        axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", main = title)
  axis(1, seq_len(k), colnames(m), las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7, tick = FALSE)
  axis(2, seq_len(k), rev(rownames(m)), las = 1, cex.axis = 0.7, tick = FALSE)
  v <- t(m[k:1, ])
  text(rep(seq_len(k), k), rep(seq_len(k), each = k), ifelse(is.na(v), "", round(v)), cex = 0.7)
}
op_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(6, 6.5, 2, 0.5))
draw_heat(pair_matrix("practice_state"), "State, % any match")
draw_heat(pair_matrix("practice_zip5"), "ZIP5, % any match")
par(op_par)
```

The two panels tell different stories. Sources mostly agree on the state, and
disagree on the ZIP. Every pair involving PECOS sits at the bottom, *including
PECOS against DAC*, which shares its lineage. PECOS lists the organization a
midwife bills through, and DAC lists where she practices, so they describe
different addresses even though both come from CMS enrollment. Shared lineage
can drive agreement up (Doximity against NPPES) or leave it unchanged, so it
has to be declared and reported, not inferred from the numbers.

### Missing is not a disagreement

For one pair, the counts below show where the midwives each source lists end
up. Only the "usable in both" row is a comparison.

```{r missing-vs-disagree}
pair_breakdown <- function(a, b, attr) {
  ua <- tapply(!is.na(usable[[a]][[attr]]), usable[[a]]$npi, any)
  ub <- tapply(!is.na(usable[[b]][[attr]]), usable[[b]]$npi, any)
  both <- intersect(names(ua), names(ub))
  c(listed_by_one_only = length(union(names(ua), names(ub))) - length(both),
    listed_by_both_but_unusable_in_one = sum(!(ua[both] & ub[both])),
    usable_in_both = sum(ua[both] & ub[both]))
}
pair_breakdown("nppes", "healthgrades", "practice_state")
```

## The error floor

If two sources disagree for a midwife, at least one is wrong for her. With
disagreement rate \(d\) among the compared midwives, the worse of the two is
wrong for at least \(d/2\) of them. The bound needs no truth. It is only a
floor, though: it does not say which source is worse, and two sources that
agree can both be wrong. Taking the floor from the upper end of the agreement
interval gives a conservative version.

```{r fig-floor, fig.height = 4.6, fig.alt = "Dot plot of the ZIP5 error floor for each of the fifteen source pairs, with Wilson-interval error bars, coloured by lineage. Pairs with PECOS have floors near 40 percent; NPPES against Doximity is lowest."}
z <- agree[agree$attribute == "practice_zip5", ]
z$floor <- (100 - z$pct_any) / 2
z$floor_lo <- (100 - ci$ci_high[agree$attribute == "practice_zip5"]) / 2
z$floor_hi <- (100 - ci$ci_low[agree$attribute == "practice_zip5"]) / 2
z <- z[order(z$floor), ]
cols <- c("separately collected" = "grey30", "shared (CMS enrollment)" = "#d95f02",
          "possible NPPES seeding" = "#7570b3")
op_par <- par(mar = c(4.5, 11, 2, 1))
plot(z$floor, seq_len(nrow(z)), xlim = c(0, 50), pch = 19, col = cols[z$lineage], yaxt = "n",
     xlab = "Worse source wrong for at least this % of compared midwives", ylab = "",
     main = "ZIP5 error floor, d/2")
segments(z$floor_lo, seq_len(nrow(z)), z$floor_hi, seq_len(nrow(z)), col = cols[z$lineage])
axis(2, seq_len(nrow(z)), paste(z$source_a, "/", z$source_b), las = 1, cex.axis = 0.7)
legend("bottomright", names(cols), col = cols, pch = 19, bty = "n", cex = 0.75)
par(op_par)
```

## Which source is the lone dissenter?

With three or more sources, `attribute_odd_one_out()` finds midwives where
exactly one source differs from a value every other source shares. It needs
one value per source, so a source listing several locations contributes its
most frequent one, which is stricter than the any-match rule above. The
second run drops DAC so that the CMS enrollment lineage votes once.

```{r odd-one-out}
primary <- function(d, attr) {
  d <- d[!is.na(d[[attr]]), ]
  tab <- aggregate(list(n = d$npi), list(npi = d$npi, value = d[[attr]]), length)
  tab <- tab[order(tab$npi, -tab$n), ]
  tab <- tab[!duplicated(tab$npi), ]
  setNames(data.frame(tab$npi, 2026, tab$value), c("npi", "year", attr))
}
odd_rates <- function(src, attr) {
  rec <- attribute_odd_one_out(lapply(usable[src], primary, attr = attr), attribute = attr)
  list(structure = table(rec$structure), rates = attribute_odd_one_out_rate(rec))
}
zip_all <- odd_rates(names(raw), "practice_zip5")
zip_all$structure
as.data.frame(zip_all$rates)
as.data.frame(odd_rates(setdiff(names(raw), "dac"), "practice_zip5")$rates)
```

```{r fig-odd, fig.height = 3.6, fig.alt = "Horizontal bars of how often each source is the lone dissenter on practice ZIP5. PECOS is the odd one out far more often than any other source; NPPES and Doximity least often."}
r <- as.data.frame(zip_all$rates)
op_par <- par(mar = c(4, 8, 2, 1))
barplot(rev(100 * r$odd_rate), names.arg = rev(r$source), horiz = TRUE, las = 1, border = NA,
        xlim = c(0, 5 * ceiling(20 * max(r$odd_rate)) + 5),
        col = "#4d4d4d", xlab = "% of eligible midwives where this source alone disagrees",
        main = "ZIP5: who is the odd one out?")
par(op_par)
```

PECOS is the lone dissenter far more often than any other source, which
fits it describing a different address. NPPES is rarely the odd one out, but
that is weak evidence for NPPES: Doximity copies it, so NPPES sitting in the
majority can be an echo rather than corroboration. Being the odd one out
says a source is out of step with the others, not that it is wrong.

## Writing it up

`attribute_oig_audit_prose()` builds an OIG-shaped results paragraph from the
completeness and agreement tables. Every number in it is read from those
tables.

```{r prose}
cat(strwrap(attribute_oig_audit_prose(
  presence, attribute_set_agreement_summary(attribute_set_agreement(set_input("practice_zip5"), "practice_zip5")),
  year = 2026, source_a = "nppes", source_b = "pecos",
  attribute = "practice_zip5", attribute_label = "practice ZIP codes"
)), sep = "\n")
```

The paragraph says "physician records" whatever the profession, and its
first sentence gives the size of the frame (here `r n`) for each source, not
the number of records present. Report the present counts from `completeness`
alongside it.

## What this does not show

- **Which source is right.** Agreement, consensus and the error floor are all
  relative. A unanimous answer can be wrong when the sources share an
  upstream feed.
- **Timing.** A midwife who moved between two sources' snapshot dates
  disagrees without either source being wrong for its own date. OIG checked
  this with two snapshot dates; `vignette("lead-lag-staleness")` does it with
  full panels.
- **Accuracy.** Estimating each source's error rate, rather than a floor on
  it, needs a verified sample. See `attribute_verification_questionnaire()`,
  `attribute_nonresponse_audit()` and `validity_estimates()`.
